thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: high tail latency and error spike observed for runtime slice rollout 2026-03-17T02:10Z. Severity: P1. Metric: p99 latency > 2.5s across canary. 

oncall_tony: On it. Which rollout id?

incident-bot: rollout_id=rl-2026-03-17-slice-A, canary=5%, affected region=us-west-2. Error class: kernel_fallback + batch_throttle. Sample trace: /v1/generate -> 502.

maria_g: I’m seeing kernel fallback churn on canary hosts: logs show repeated kernel swap to "quant_fallback" then prefetch queue backlog.

maria_g: snippet: ```
2026-03-17T02:09:41Z host-12 runtime WARN kernel_switch(reason=OOM_KVCACHE)
2026-03-17T02:09:41Z host-12 runtime INFO kernel=quant_fallback slot_swap=3
2026-03-17T02:09:42Z host-12 batcher WARN queue_len=120 -> throttle
```

ajohnson: Do we have a kill-switch flag for this rollout? If it's causing kernel fallbacks we should flip ASAP.

oncall_tony: There is a feature flag rollouts.slice-A.enabled in config. I can flip to off for canary. That will stop new traffic to the slice.

devin: Customer impact: monitoring shows an increase in 502/504 errors to a small set of high-throughput customers on dedicated pools. Rough numbers: ~0.8% of requests failing, p99 latency from 1.1s -> 3.2s for affected slice.

cs_ryan: Heads up - Support is already getting a couple of tickets from a fintech customer in us-west-2. They reported timeouts around 02:11Z. Need a short blurb to send.

oncall_tony: Action: flipping rollouts.slice-A.enabled -> false now. Will route canary traffic back to previous slice.

incident-bot: Command received: flip_flag rollouts.slice-A.enabled=false by oncall_tony at 5167890220. Canary traffic draining.

maria_g: After flip: kernel fallback events dropped on hosts that were serving slice-A. Prefetch queue reduced to ~10 within 40s.

jamie: Nice. Do we still need a rollback of the release or can we re-run with adjusted batching config?

elena_ops: Canary was 5% only, so widespread customer impact is limited, but I recommend we do a canary rollback and iterate on batch window and prefetch limits before re-promoting. Also suggest enabling the legacy kernel affinity to avoid quant fallback.

oncall_tony: Agreed. Rolling back rl-2026-03-17-slice-A to previous image now (rollback started at 5167890305).

sre_bot: Auto-check: rollback accepted on 3/3 canary hosts. Metrics watch created: p99 latency, error-rate, kernel_fallback_count. Alert threshold lowered for 30m.

devin: Confirming customer impact mitigation: error rate dropping to baseline in us-west-2. Will keep monitoring for any retries causing user-visible duplicates.

cs_ryan: Blurb for support: "We detected a canary regression affecting a small subset of requests in us-west-2. Traffic was routed back to the previous version; we are monitoring and will follow up with root cause. If you see retries or duplicates, please let us know."

jamie: Assigning postmortem: owner=maria_g, timeline owner=ajohnson. Postmortem to include: batch window config, kernel affinity changes, how rollout tooling gated canary.

oncall_tony: Handoff: I'm staying on for 20m to watch metrics, then handing to night oncall = ajohnson. If anything flares, page pager channel.

ajohnson: Ack - will take over at 5167890456. I’ll keep the incident channel updated and start the RCA ticket.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to mitigation state. No active customer outages post-rollback. Monitoring retention watch set for 2h.
